text: The Bridletowne Neighbourhood Centre/Community Hub is a long-standing City-building initiative that will bring much-needed community space, programs and services to the Finch-Warden/Steeles-L’Amoreaux/Bridletowne area. For more than a decade, City Council has supported the use of the City-owned lands at 1355 Bridletowne Circle to create a multi-service community hub. The City acquired the property in 2011 for approximately $5.9 million, and the proposed nominal transfer of the 5.2-acre site to the YMCA of Greater Toronto represents a significant City contribution toward unlocking long-planned community infrastructure in an area of significant need. While Scarborough Health Network is no longer advancing its component of the project, the YMCA of Greater Toronto remains committed to moving the project forward with United Way Greater Toronto and other community partners. City Council reaffirm the City’s commitment to the development of the Bridletowne Neighbourhood Centre through the transfer of 5.2 acres of the northerly portion of the property municipally known as 1355 Bridletowne Circle to the Young Men's Christian Association of Greater Toronto, as originally approved by City Council under Item 2011.EX9.16 , to deliver a community-serving hub that will include community agency space, youth and family programming and health and fitness services, provided such transaction can be completed by October 31, 2026. 2.
